neighbours.label: continuative/habitual verb or adverb in older narrative prose ('kept up', 'kept alive', 'as is often said')
fire: Through the long winter the garrison kept up a steady watch on the river.
The old monks kept alive the art of copying manuscripts by hand.
The war was not, as is often claimed, a simple quarrel over land.
All through the siege the gunners kept firing at the walls.
The widow kept to her room and mourned for many weeks.
The scouts, as was generally believed, had already crossed the pass.
Despite the storm the crew kept on rowing toward the shore.
The tribe kept up its ancient customs long after the traders came.
quiet: Through the long winter the garrison watched the river from the tower.
The old monks copied manuscripts by hand in the cold library.
The war was a quarrel over land between two noble families.
During the siege the gunners fired at the walls at dawn.
The widow went to her room and wrote a letter to her son.
The scouts had already crossed the pass before the snow fell.
In the storm the crew rowed toward the shore with all their strength.
The tribe held a feast when the traders arrived in spring.
